sections.title: Large deviation estimate for predictable quadratic variation of M_{x,n}
Limit Laplace transform of the Busemann cocycle
Second-order expansion below the drift without exponential moment

results.content_role: main second-order expansion: lim_{lambda->0} (Lambda(lambda)-lambda l_mu)/lambda^2 = sigma_mu^2/2 for the displacement d(z_n,o), under finite exponential moment
results.author_proof: no proof at this point; proved through the general form Theorem 4.1 (roadmap lines 152-154, reduction to x=o at line 733)

results.content_role: three enumerated notes: (1) the Busemann-cocycle version is Theorem 4.1; (2) bounded support allows replacing d(z_n,o) by the translation distance tau (cites BMSS Th. 1.3); (3) sigma_mu>0 iff mu non-arithmetic (cites Remark 3.7 and Benoist--Quint)
results.author_proof: none (no proof environment; assertions referred to other results)

results.content_role: rate function expansion lim_{lambda->0} I(l_mu+lambda)/lambda^2 = 1/(2 sigma_mu^2) for the LDP rate function I of (1.4)
results.author_proof: prose proof in subsection 4.4, lines 909-920, closing with qed at line 920 (no proof environment)

results.content_role: role of hyperbolicity (Lemma 3.1 with the cohomological equation, Lemma 3.8) and possible extensions (cites horbez, choi, choi1, choi2)
results.author_proof: none

results.content_role: Freedman's submartingale transform for bounded increments, quoted with attribution [Freedman, Cor. 1.4(b), (3.7) and (3.9)]; item 2 is noted at line 216 as a consequence of item 1
results.author_proof: none in this paper; external cited result (no proof environment follows)

results.content_role: new exponential submartingale transform: exp(lambda M_n - (f(lambda a)/a^2) G_n^a) is a submartingale for submartingales whose cumulative absolute increments have finite exponential moment; G_n^a defined at lines 194-195, f(lambda)=e^{-lambda}-1+lambda
results.author_proof: complete author proof, proof environment lines 231-283 (four cases, key inequality (2.2) at lines 232-234, adapted from Freedman's Prop. 3.6)
results.split_note: This is the only part of the paper that is a self-contained general martingale result independent of the hyperbolic setting. It is used essentially only for the lower bound of the main theorem, so by default it belongs to the main core rather than a separate candidate; listed here so the decision is explicit.

results.content_role: Benoist--Quint martingale decomposition sigma(L_n,x) - n l_mu = M_{x,n} + O_{x,n}(1) with the remainder bounded uniformly in n and x
results.author_proof: proof environment lines 387-401, but existence of the bounded psi (cocycle equation (3.1), line 397) is attributed to [BQ.hyperbolic Prop. 4.6], [horbez] and [aoun-sert]; only the martingale property is verified here (lines 398-400)

results.content_role: two-sided bound n l_mu - C <= E[sigma(L_n,x)] <= n l_mu + C
results.author_proof: none stated; one-line consequence of E[M_{x,n}]=0, no proof environment

results.content_role: exponential large deviation estimate for the predictable quadratic variation <M_x>_n around n sigma_mu^2, uniformly in the starting point
results.author_proof: no single proof environment: reduction prose lines 438-448 (additive functional phi, (3.6)-(3.7)); the result is then assembled from Proposition 3.4 and Lemma 3.6, with line 518 asserting that hypothesis (3.4) holds for phi

results.content_role: BQ.CLT Prop. 3.1 modified: LDP for additive functionals of a Markov chain under uniform Cesaro convergence (3.4) of (1/n) sum P^j phi, with the continuity assumption on phi dropped
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 461-511, self-described as adaptation of Benoist--Quint's proof; enclosed in \Changel (line 450) / \Changelback (line 512), which are typesetting macros only

results.content_role: sufficient condition (compact E, Feller P, continuous phi with unique average) for the uniform Cesaro hypothesis
results.author_proof: none (discussion with citations)

results.content_role: uniform convergence of f_n(x) = (1/n) sum_{j<=n} P_mu^j phi(x) to sigma_mu^2, with formula (3.10) and independence of the stationary measure nu
results.author_proof: proof environment lines 553-627, explicitly headed 'Proof of Lemma 3.6' and placed after Lemma 3.8, which it uses; Burkholder inequality, L^4 uniform integrability, (3.16)

results.content_role: sigma_mu=0 iff kappa(g)-n l_mu is uniformly bounded on supp mu^{*n}; sigma_mu>0 iff mu non-arithmetic; definition of non-arithmetic via the translation distance
results.author_proof: none (attributed to the argument in [BQ.hyperbolic Th. 4.7.b])

results.content_role: uniform punctual deviations P(kappa(L_k)-sigma(L_k,x) > R) <= C e^{-beta R} for all k, x in the horofunction compactification and R>0
results.author_proof: proof environment lines 540-551: reduce to [BMSS Prop. 2.12] via x_n -> x and dominated convergence

results.content_role: Laplace control of the truncated variation: lim_{a->+inf} limsup_{lambda->0+} (1/lambda) limsup_n (1/n) log E[exp(-lambda(G_n^a - n sigma_mu^2))] = 0
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 639-717: Cauchy--Schwarz plus estimates (3.11) and (3.12)

results.content_role: general Busemann-cocycle form: for every x in the horofunction compactification, both liminf and limsup Laplace transforms satisfy (Lambda_x^{+-}(lambda)-l lambda)/lambda^2 -> sigma_mu^2/2
results.author_proof: no proof environment; proved by Proposition 4.2 (all lambda) and Proposition 4.3 (lambda->0 upper bound); roadmap at line 743

results.content_role: lower bound lim_{lambda->0} (Lambda_x^-(lambda)-l_mu lambda)/lambda^2 >= sigma_mu^2/2
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 755-814: Proposition 2.2, Holder splitting with p>1, then Corollary 3.9; lambda<0 obtained by replacing M_x with -M_x

results.content_role: upper bound lim_{lambda->0} (Lambda_x^+(lambda)-l_mu lambda)/lambda^2 <= sigma_mu^2/2
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 884-907: Proposition 4.4 yields v(mu), then the acceleration trick over mu^{*k} with (4.5) v(mu^{*k})/k -> sigma_mu^2 from Lemma 3.6

results.content_role: subgaussian bound E[exp(lambda(sigma(L_n,x)-n l_mu))] <= exp(lambda^2 (v(mu)+eps) n/2 + C|lambda|), with v(mu)=sup_xi E[M_{xi,1}^2]
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 863-875: iterate the tower property from Lemma 4.5, then absorb the bounded remainder

results.content_role: deterministic conditional-exponential bound E[exp(lambda Delta_n M_x)|F_{n-1}] <= exp(lambda^2 (v(mu)+eps)/2) for |lambda|<b
results.author_proof: complete author proof lines 843-861: third-order Taylor expansion, exponential moment, cocycle decomposition

results.content_role: comparison with Bennett--Bernstein literature for unbounded differences (de la Pena, DZ, fan.grama.liu, Liu--Watbled) and why Lemma 4.5 suffices here
results.author_proof: none

results.content_role: on finite-time large deviation estimates; asserts Chernoff bounds from Proposition 4.4 and, in the footnote at line 923, that these give lim_{lambda->0} I(l_mu+lambda)/lambda^2 >= 1/(2 sigma_mu^2) via acceleration
results.author_proof: none; finite-time statement and footnote implication are asserted, not derived

results.content_role: open question: is Lambda_x^+ = Lambda_x^- for every x in the horofunction boundary, and do the transforms agree near 0 for different starting points
results.author_proof: none; discussion and an F_2 example at line 935

results.content_role: open question: under finite second moment, is lim_{lambda->0-} I(lambda+l_mu)/lambda^2 = 1/(2 sigma_mu^2); related discussion for sigma_mu^2=infinity at line 946
results.author_proof: none
